mysql.name: MySQL
mysql.summary: Run by Oracle, with Long Term Support releases (8.4 and 9.7) and a native binary JSON type.
mysql.bestWhen: You host on Azure, want binary JSON, or have an app written for MySQL 8.x.
mysql.watchOut: Its thread pool needs the paid Enterprise Edition, and one company, Oracle, sets its roadmap.

mariadb.name: MariaDB
mariadb.summary: Governed by the MariaDB Foundation, with a built-in thread pool and extra storage engines.
mariadb.bestWhen: You want foundation governance, a built-in thread pool, or a gradual move from MySQL.
mariadb.watchOut: It no longer swaps in cleanly for current MySQL, its JSON is stored as text, and Azure retired its managed MariaDB.

postgres.name: PostgreSQL
postgres.summary: A separate project, not a MySQL fork, with a binary jsonb type that can be indexed.
postgres.bestWhen: Indexed binary JSON matters most and you are not tied to the MySQL family.
postgres.watchOut: Moving to it is a migration, not an upgrade, and MySQL tooling does not carry over.
